newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends quiet session mostly firmer.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends quiet session mostly firmer.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended the week on a quiet note, finishing mostly firmer on Friday, as locals beefed up their long positions ahead of the weekend, trading sources said.
Light origin selling capped gains, they added, and kept prices fairly rangebound.
"It was an inside trading day," one dealer said. "Locals did most of the buying. They tried to run it up, but there was some origin selling toward the highs."
Benchmark July rose 1.00 cents per lb on the day, to 218.00 cents, after ranging between 218.50 and 214.75. The back months closed 1.05 higher to 1.00 lower.
Spot May suffered losses for the second straight day, as operators continued to liquidate and roll positions forward ahead of the spot month's expiry on May 19.
May fell 1.00 cent, to 239.00 cents, shrinking the May/July switch to 21.10 cents from 23.10 cents at the close on Thursday.
With May open interest falling to 512 lots as of Thursday, most traders expect the spot month to go off the board in a fairly orderly fashion.
The July/September switch was fairly steady, ending at 22.35 cents compared with 22.40 cents on Thursday.

On the charts, traders pegged near-term July resistance at 219.00-220.00, followed by 225.00, its life-of-contract high. July near-term support was seen at 214.50, followed by a strong downside hurdle at 209.00.
On the fundamental side, portworkers at Brazil's key port of Santos returned to work on Friday after a one-day strike to protest at a delay in receiving their full April salary.
Union officials said Friday the portworkers are not considering any further action until they see whether the CODESP port authority fulfills its promise to pay outstanding April salaries on May 13.
After Friday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks increased by 1,500 bags, to 26,919 bags as of May 8. There were 16,615 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.

Despite the modest certified stock build, traders said consumer coffee inventories were still extremely low. They said continued supply worries -- most notably in second-largest producer Colombia -- and the onset of the Brazilian winter should keep prices well underpinned.
Traders await the CFTC Commitment of Traders report due late Friday. They expected the data to show an increase in speculative long positions.

They noted, however, speculative interest in the coffee market has dropped off since late March, when total open interest peaked at some 42,000 lots. As of May 8, total open interest stood at 29,480 lots, down 602 lots from the preivious session.
Volume reached an estimated 5,747 lots on the day.
